_README: Every question the welcome interview asks, in one machine-readable file.
WHY THIS EXISTS: onboarding is a conversation, but a conversation isn't
repeatable. Fill this in once and you can rebuild the whole system from
scratch — stamp, hand the lead this file, done — then tear it down and do
it again identically. That makes onboarding testable instead of a
one-shot interview you hope went right.
HOW TO USE IT (three ways, all valid):
1. Ignore it. DM the lead and answer conversationally. This file is
never required.
2. Fill it in first, then tell the lead: 'my answers are in
<path>/onboarding-answers.json'. It reads, confirms the summary with
you, and persists — no interview.
3. Fill in part of it. The lead uses what's here and asks only about
what's missing or null.
NEVER PUT A SECRET IN THIS FILE. No API keys, tokens, passwords, or
webhook URLs — ever. Secrets live only in the OneCLI vault; this file is
config (repo names, channel names, ids, preferences). It is safe to commit
to a private repo, and scripts/check-onboarding-keys.sh fails if anything
in it looks like a credential.
'persists_to' tells you where each answer ends up. config.env keys are
read by bash gate scripts; project_config keys are prose the agent reads,
four of which setup-check.sh greps literally. Getting these two namespaces
backwards is the #1 cause of 'I answered that but nothing happened'.

decide_before_stamping._note: These two shape how tasks get created. Answering them late is expensive — see docs/INSTALL.md step 2.

timezone._ask: What timezone should scheduled work land in? Schedules are cron lines in task frontmatter and the kit pins TZ=UTC; changing a time after stamping means cancel-and-recreate per task.
timezone._action_if_not_utc: Edit the schedule: lines in your local copy of the 18 task files BEFORE stamping.

agents_to_stamp._ask: Which agents do you want? 'support' (the lead) is required; engineering and marketing are optional and can be added or paused later.

primary_github_repo._ask: The project's main GitHub repo — everything else is inferred from this. Format owner/repo.

repo_map._ask: Per function: which repo, and a subpath if it isn't the repo root. Functions often SHARE one repo — docs and site are frequently subdirectories of product. Don't assume separate repos.
_derives: config.env:COMMUNITY_REPOS — space-separated list of repos to TRIAGE (issues/PRs/advisories/metrics). Normally every repo here, but it's the owner's call. Set on the lead AND coding.

config.env:MIRROR_REPOS — space-separated list of ALL repos above (including wiki, including ones sharing a repo) for repo-mirror-sync to keep checked out. Superset of COMMUNITY_REPOS; falls back to it if unset. Coding only.
config.env:CONTENT_REPO — the marketing function's repo, where content drafts get committed and PR'd. Marketing only; content-draft-cycle and draft-cleanup both hard-require it.

wiki._note: A GitHub wiki is a real repo named owner/repo.wiki. Use null if the project has none.

triage_repos_override._ask: Optional: if you DON'T want every repo above triaged, list just the ones you do. Leave null to triage all of them.
triage_repos_override._note: Only changes COMMUNITY_REPOS. MIRROR_REPOS always covers the full map — mirroring is cheap and read-only.

docs_site_url._ask: Where you point people for how-to answers

topic_scope._ask: What's on-topic; anything else gets a friendly redirect

goals._ask: Which of the four jobs are goals for this project? Each yes makes a set of tasks eligible; each no keeps them paused. See welcome/SKILL.md step 3 for the task mapping.

audience_priority._ask: If growth is a goal: which audiences, in priority order?

github_bot_username._ask: The dedicated bot account's GitHub username — NEVER the owner's own. Every token is checked against this mechanically.
github_bot_username._note: Needs to land in BOTH namespaces: the scripts read the uppercase env key, setup-check.sh greps the lowercase prose key.

discord_display_name._ask: The Discord application's display name. Make it visibly match the GitHub bot username — this is the only agent with a public voice on both platforms, and a mismatched pair reads as two different bots.

channels._ask: Which Discord channels belong to which tier. Tier decides engage-mode, not per-message judgment.

support_auto_reply._note: Replies without being @mentioned. Needs --sender-scope all at wiring time.

announcements_channel._ask: If the team-lead tier has more than one channel, which is THE announcements channel? release-announcement-watch needs one unambiguous target.

discord_invite_url._ask: Invite URL to offer from GitHub replies when real-time chat would help, or null

maintainers._ask: Who counts as a maintainer for decisions the agent must not make

escalation_backstop._ask: The second human — name and contact — who takes abuse reports and urgent escalations when you're unreachable.
escalation_backstop._note: Going live without one is recorded as an open risk, not silently accepted. Code-of-conduct response is a human role everywhere it's done seriously — never an agent's.

target_audience._ask: Who is your content actually for, in your own words? e.g. 'church administrative staff and volunteer teams' — not 'developers' unless that's genuinely true.
target_audience._note: Marketing writes for this. Without it, drafts default to generic SaaS copy and the no-jargon rule has nothing to anchor to.

tone._ask: The register that follows from that audience, e.g. 'warm, practical, no engineering jargon'

docs_style._ask: Current-state only, or is version-history language ('added in 2.1') fine?

brand_source_repo._ask: Repo holding brand voice / content pillars / calendar, if different from the content repo

release_watch_repo._ask: Which repo's releases should trigger content drafting? Usually the product repo.
release_watch_repo._note: Unset means content-draft-cycle loses its release trigger and only fires on its weekly floor. If this differs from the content repo, the marketing token's repo-access list must include BOTH.

social._ask: Platforms this project has (for the follower series), which ones it posts to, and how each publishes.

profiles._format: list of public profile URLs — read-only, no credential

_mechanisms.intent-url: free, no key, DEFAULT — agent drafts, human clicks Post in a pre-filled composer
_mechanisms.paid-api: costs real money and is opt-in only; X has no free tier since Feb 2026 (~$0.20/link-post). Even enabled, the agent holds no posting credential — an OneCLI request-hold keeps a human button-press in the loop.

ga4_property_id._ask: GA4 numeric property id, or null for 'not now'

posthog_host._note: The script defaults to US. An EU project MUST set this or every call hits the wrong region.

onecli_dashboard_url._ask: What URL should the agent give you for the OneCLI vault dashboard — this machine, or a reachable remote address (e.g. a Tailscale IP) for checking in from elsewhere?
onecli_dashboard_url._note: 127.0.0.1 only resolves on the sandbox host. If you'll ever check from a phone or another laptop, give the reachable address instead.

workspace_backup_repo._ask: Private repo the lead pushes its workspace to, or null to skip
workspace_backup_repo._note: This is the only thing that survives a sandbox recreate.

github_actions_notifications._ask: Set up deterministic label→Discord notifications in CI? See examples/github-discord-notify.yml

gfi_label._ask: Your beginner-friendly issue label, if it isn't 'good first issue'

shared_inbox._ask: Shared project inbox address, or null. inbox-check stays paused until an email MCP is actually connected.

models._ask: Confirm or override the per-agent model tier. Never Opus-class on a scheduled task.
